186: class Sample:
187:     """takes a random sample of the values
188: 
189:     >>> glom([1, 2, 3], Group(Sample(2)))  # doctest: +SKIP
190:     [1, 3]
191:     >>> glom(range(5000), Group(Sample(2)))  # doctest: +SKIP
192:     [272, 2901]
193: 
194:     The advantage of this over :func:`random.sample` is that this can
195:     take an arbitrarily-sized, potentially-very-long streaming input
196:     and returns a fixed-size output. Note that this does not stream
197:     results out, so your streaming input must have finite length.
198:     """

209:         num_seen, sample = tree[self]
210:         if len(sample) < self.size:
211:             sample.append(target)
212:         else:
213:             pos = random.randint(0, num_seen)
214:             if pos < self.size:
215:                 sample[pos] = target
216:         tree[self][0] += 1
217:         return sample

224: class Limit:
225:     """
226:     Limits the number of values passed to sub-accumulator
227: 
228:     >>> glom([1, 2, 3], Group(Limit(2)))
229:     [1, 2]
230: 
231:     To override the default untransformed list output, set the subspec kwarg:
232: 
233:     >>> glom(range(10), Group(Limit(3, subspec={(lambda x: x % 2): [T]})))
234:     {0: [0, 2], 1: [1]}
235: 
236:     You can even nest Limits in other ``Group`` specs:
237: 
238:     >>> glom(range(10), Group(Limit(5, {(lambda x: x % 2): Limit(2)})))
239:     {0: [0, 2], 1: [1, 3]}
240: 
241:     """
242:     __slots__ = ('n', 'subspec')
243: 
244:     def __init__(self, n, subspec=_MISSING):
245:         if subspec is _MISSING:
246:             subspec = [T]
247:         self.n = n
248:         self.subspec = subspec
249: 
250:     def glomit(self, target, scope):
251:         if scope[MODE] is not GROUP:
252:             raise BadSpec("Limit() only valid in Group mode")
253:         tree = scope[ACC_TREE]  # current accumulator support structure
254:         if self not in tree:
255:             tree[self] = [0, {}]
256:         scope[ACC_TREE] = tree[self][1]
257:         tree[self][0] += 1
258:         if tree[self][0] > self.n:
259:             return STOP
260:         return scope[glom](target, self.subspec, scope)
261: 
262:     def __repr__(self):
263:         return f'{self.__class__.__name__}({self.n!r}, {self.subspec!r})'
